item.title: How to grow a tea garden at home
item.description: Nothing beats the satisfaction of having a nice cup of tea – except maybe sipping a custom blend you grew and harvested from your very own garden. The Peninsula is suitable for cultivating many edible plants that can be used for delicious and nutritious teas, according to local garden experts. The post How to grow a tea garden at home appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: Palo Alto fights federal plan to speed up cell tower approval
item.description: As Palo Alto prepares to expand its fiber network system, the city is also fighting a new proposal by the federal government that would make it earlier for telecommunication companies to install their own wireless facilities, even in the face of local objections. The post Palo Alto fights federal plan to speed up cell tower approval appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: Sugar, Dopamine, and the Long Way to Freedom
item.description: It’s been 37 years since someone first told me, “You change personalities when you eat sugar.” The post Sugar, Dopamine, and the Long Way to Freedom appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: East Palo Alto residents to get easier access to Bay Trail
item.description: The City of East Palo Alto, in partnership with the Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District, began constructing on Tuesday a new entrance point to the Bay Trail at the end of Rutgers Street, a project that will give local residents easy access to the trail system. The post East Palo Alto residents to get easier access to Bay Trail appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: Feds expected in South Bay during Super Bowl 60
item.description: Federal agents are anticipated to be in the South Bay ahead of the Super Bowl, as the nation grapples with increased violence related to immigration enforcement. The post Feds expected in South Bay during Super Bowl 60 appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: TheatreWorks seeks ‘permanent home’ at redeveloped Cubberley
item.description: The city of Palo Alto and TheatreWorks Silicon Valley announced this morning that they are exploring a partnership to create a performing arts center with two theaters at Cubberley Community Center, a project that city leaders hope will energize their broader effort to renovate the eclectic community hub. The post TheatreWorks seeks ‘permanent home’ at redeveloped Cubberley appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: Update: Downtown Palo Alto Peet’s store may reopen after closure
item.description: The Peet’s Coffee on Homer Avenue in downtown Palo Alto is one of dozens of locations set to close on Friday, as the company remains in the process of an $18 billion acquisition by Keurig Dr. Pepper. The post Update: Downtown Palo Alto Peet’s store may reopen after closure appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: County health care system braces for ‘fiscal emergency’ from federal funding cuts
item.description: Santa Clara Valley Healthcare, the county’s public health care system, is preparing to eliminate 218 positions, maximize reimbursement from insurers to increase revenue, and consolidate patient care such as cardiac services as part of a strategy for dealing with massive federal cuts. The post County health care system braces for ‘fiscal emergency’ from federal funding cuts appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: Historic Woodside restaurant reopens as flower shop and cafe with Michelin cred chef
item.description: Nearly every day for five years, Aubriana Kasper drove by the olive-tinted facade of The Little Store in Woodside. Most recently, the building — identified by an eponymous wood sign celebrating its standing since 1902 — was used as a test kitchen for Hero Bread, but hadn’t been open to the public for years. The post Historic Woodside restaurant reopens as flower shop and cafe with Michelin cred chef appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: The Pro opens in downtown Palo Alto, carrying on a 58-year legacy
item.description: A longtime Palo Alto sports bar has been reborn. The Old Pro, a community watering hole since 1964, shuttered in 2022. But on Monday, it reopened with a new look, menu and mascot (and even a podcasting studio), while still paying homage to its predecessor. The post The Pro opens in downtown Palo Alto, carrying on a 58-year legacy appeared first on Palo Alto Online.
